record.title: How to Create an Emergency Water Supply
record.locator: How much; Choosing a container; Cleaning; Storing; Using
record.finding: Emergency baseline: at least one gallon/person/day for three days; aim for two weeks and allow additional needs. Use suitable food-grade containers, never former toxic-chemical containers. Wash, sanitize with one teaspoon of 5-9% bleach per quart, wet all surfaces for 30 seconds, empty and air-dry. Fill with safe water, close tightly, date and keep cool, shaded and away from chemicals; replace home-filled water six-monthly. Handle hygienically. Unopened commercial water is a reliable emergency choice.

record.title: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency
record.locator: Overview; Boil; Disinfect; Filtering; Using light
record.finding: Boiling clear water for one minute, or three above 6,500 feet, is the standard germ-control method. Let cloudy water settle or prefilter it. Bleach needs at least 30 minutes and concentration-specific dosing. Disinfectants are less effective for some parasites. Boiling and disinfection do not remove toxic chemicals. Ordinary filters may not remove all germs. Iodine is unsuitable for certain groups and extended use. Safe water is needed for food, dishes, teeth and hygiene.

record.title: How to Find Clean Water in an Emergency
record.locator: Inside the home; Outside the home
record.finding: Pool/spa water may serve hygiene and cleaning but is not drinking water. Outdoor sources can contain pathogens and chemicals; assess and treat them. Avoid fuel- or toxic-chemical-contaminated water for drinking and bathing.

record.title: About Choosing Home Water Filters
record.locator: Many filters do not remove germs; Do not rely on taste or smell; Test; Understand pore size
record.finding: Match treatment to tested contaminants and certified performance; ordinary carbon taste filters generally do not remove germs. Appearance and flavor do not prove safety. Test private well/rain supplies and follow system maintenance. Absolute and nominal pore ratings differ.

record.title: About Home Water Treatment Systems
record.finding: RO and distillation can remove many germs and dissolved contaminants, but removal is system- and contaminant-specific. Distillation fails to remove some volatile compounds, solvents and pesticides. Treatment choice should follow water testing.

record.title: Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water
record.finding: For clear water EPA lists eight drops of 6% or six drops of 8.25% bleach per gallon, doubled for cloudy, colored or very cold water; wait 30 minutes, repeat if no slight chlorine odor then wait 15 more. Use fresh plain suitable bleach. HTH stock: heaping teaspoon in two gallons, then 1:100 (one pint per 12.5 gallons), with ventilation and eye protection. 2% iodine: five drops/quart clear or ten cloudy; wait 30 minutes. Tablets follow labels. These methods do not remove dissolved chemicals.

record.title: Order WaterBOB: instructions and FAQ
record.finding: Manufacturer recommends one-time use. Capacity is up to 100 gallons, limited by tub; do not fill above its rim. Tub is recommended for spill containment and convenience; manufacturer says the bladder can support itself. Instructions describe unfolding, faucet filling and dispensing with included pump. Storage claims are conditional, and the FAQ contains inconsistent four- and sixteen-week language; no duration guarantee is adopted here.

record.title: Collecting Rainwater and Your Health
record.locator: Health risks; Recommendations; Improve your system
record.finding: Rain may contain germs and chemicals from air, roofs and collection materials. Match quality to use; avoid contaminating potable plumbing. Maintain and test systems. Prefer safer supplies for ingestion and food uses; debris diversion does not alone make rain potable.

record.title: 12VAC5-635-240 Design and installation
record.finding: Regulated systems require prefiltration, an automatic accessible first-flush device after prefiltration, protected storage openings and defined inlet/outlet arrangements. This section does not prescribe the book's four-inch diversion quantity. Applicability and rain-barrel exclusions must be assessed separately.

record.title: Rainwater Harvesting
record.locator: BIG PICTURE; non-potable and POTABLE use questions
record.finding: Virginia permits regulated potable rainwater systems under Tier 4 construction and operating approvals. Rain barrels are excluded from the regulations. Other new nonpotable systems have registration obligations, and building/local rules still apply. No general tax-credit entitlement is established by this page.

record.title: 12VAC5-630-410 Construction; general
record.locator: B Well bore; C Casing; D Screens; F Grouting
record.finding: Well design depends on geology. Casing protects bore and water quality; screen dimensions depend on formation analysis. Private wells require grouting, with class-specific casing and completion requirements. A bag and uncontrolled mud backfill are not demonstrated compliance.

record.title: 13VAC5-63-210: residential nonpotable gray water provisions
record.locator: P2910 and P2911 amendments, especially P2911.1.1, .2, .4 and .6
record.finding: Graywater systems need separation from potable plumbing, use-specific quality and filtration/disinfection where required, approved bypass and backwater provisions. Untreated graywater tank retention is limited to 24 hours. Building plumbing approval does not remove VDH/DEQ responsibilities for treatment and discharge.

record.title: How Do Hydrologists Locate Groundwater?
record.finding: Groundwater occupies pores and cracks in soils and rocks. Hydrogeologic maps, nearby well records, testing and chemical analysis inform quantity and quality. Valleys and water-loving plants may offer clues, without guaranteeing usable water. Neither fixed drilling depth nor surface clues replace investigation.

record.title: Household Water Treatment
record.finding: Designed slow-sand treatment includes fine sand, support gravel, underdrains and regulated flow. This description does not validate the book's gravel-sand-carbon bucket design as a pathogen barrier.

record.title: 12VAC5-630-220 Permits and inspection statement
record.finding: Private wells must meet regulations; construction, alteration, deepening and abandonment require written permission, with stated exceptions. Operation generally requires an inspection statement. Emergency or DIY intent does not itself create an exemption.

record.title: 12VAC5-630-431 Water quality
record.finding: Class III drinking-water wells require disinfection and bacteriological examination by an accredited laboratory under specified interpretation rules. Class IV nonconsumption wells are exempt from this section's water-quality requirements; a negative coliform result is not a complete chemical screen.

record.title: Water Dowsing
record.locator: What does science say about dowsing?
record.finding: Apparent dowsing success can reflect widespread groundwater; scientific location of depth, quantity and quality requires hydrologic, geologic and geophysical investigation.

record.title: Discussion on Humidity
record.finding: Warm air can contain more vapor; with unchanged moisture, warming reduces relative humidity and cooling raises it. Dew point better represents actual moisture content than relative humidity alone.

record.title: Fix a Leak Week
record.locator: Checking for Leaks; Toilet Leaks; Faucet Leaks
record.finding: Inspect for household leaks and repair faulty fixtures and seals to conserve water; the specific cause of a leak requires diagnosis.

record.title: Potable Water Reuse and Drinking Water
record.finding: Potable reuse requires treatment within drinking-water and water-quality protections. Indirect reuse includes an environmental buffer before drinking-water treatment. Ordinary wastewater discharge and validated potable reuse are different treatment endpoints.

record.title: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency
record.finding: Clear water: rolling boil one minute, three above 6500 feet; cool and protect. Prefilter cloudiness. Chemical disinfectants require specific dosing and contact time. Many portable filters do not remove viruses. UV depends on clear water and device instructions. Boiling/disinfection does not remove fuel, toxic chemicals or radioactivity.

record.title: How to Create an Emergency Water Supply
record.finding: Store at least one gallon per person daily for three days; aim for two weeks, allowing extra needs. Use suitable food-grade vessels, never toxic-chemical containers. Wash, sanitize with one teaspoon of 5-9% unscented bleach per quart, wet surfaces at least 30 seconds, empty and air-dry. Fill with safe water, close, date, keep cool/shaded and replace home-filled water six-monthly.

record.title: Collecting Rainwater and Your Health
record.finding: Roof runoff can contain germs and chemicals from air, surfaces and materials. Match quality to use, test and treat drinking supplies, maintain collection and prevent cross-contamination of potable plumbing. Water clarity or ordinary filters do not establish safety.

record.title: About Choosing Home Water Filters
record.locator: Many filters do not remove germs; Test; Pore size
record.finding: Most household carbon taste filters do not remove germs. Test for contaminants and match treatment performance to them. Smell, appearance and taste do not reliably indicate safety. Filter ratings and operating limits matter.

record.title: Rainwater Harvesting
record.finding: Roof rainwater is distinguished from ground-contact stormwater. Specified Tier-1 rain barrels are excluded from the rainwater-system regulations. Private potable Tier-4 systems require construction and operating permits, compliant design and ongoing operation/testing. Building/local requirements and backup water continuity still matter.

record.title: Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency
record.finding: Keep cold-storage doors closed; an unopened refrigerator normally protects food for four hours, a full freezer 48 and half-full freezer 24. Use thermometers and safe cold sources. Do not taste food to test safety; discard unsafe perishables. Preservation does not rescue spoiled food.

record.title: Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water
record.finding: Use fresh plain suitable bleach, product-concentration-specific dose and contact time. EPA lists eight drops of 6% or six drops of 8.25% per gallon of clear water, double for cloudy/colored/very cold water; wait 30 minutes, and if no slight chlorine odor repeat and wait 15 more. This is microbial treatment, not chemical removal. EPA's altitude threshold differs from CDC; this examination adopts CDC's threshold explicitly.

record.publisher: USDA guidance via National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: Soups
record.finding: Use ingredients that already have canning recommendations and the tested soup process. Do not add pasta, rice, flour, cream, milk or other thickeners. Soup is processed in a pressure canner using jar-size, altitude and equipment-specific controls. A sealed jar or long boiling-water treatment does not substitute for this process.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: Jerky
record.locator: Safe handling; heating and drying methods
record.finding: Raw meat can carry pathogens; safe jerky requires controlled handling and validated heating/drying. The guidance provides methods using a 160 F internal-temperature control and defined drying/storage directions. Sun exposure, optional salt/vinegar and brittle texture are not a validated kill step. This examination does not adopt the page's freezing advice for all wild-game parasites.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: General Information on Pickling
record.finding: Use tested proportions and specified vinegar acidity, generally 5%; do not alter vinegar/water/food proportions or use unknown-acidity vinegar. Fermented-product salt levels are safety controls. Use the tested product's processing and storage directions rather than an unmeasured hot-fill recipe.

record.title: Candle Fire Safety
record.finding: Prefer flashlights for power outages. If candles are used, choose stable holders, keep at least 12 inches from combustibles, extinguish before leaving or sleeping, and avoid bedrooms, bathrooms and sleeping areas. Historical candle use is not a reason to prefer flames over electric emergency lights.

record.title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning Basics
record.locator: What it is; Reducing risk; Chimneys; Generators
record.finding: CO is colorless and odorless. Use battery-backed CO alarms and properly maintained vented fuel equipment. Never heat the home with a gas oven, burn charcoal or operate camp stoves indoors. Generators must operate outside more than 20 feet from windows, doors and vents; open garage doors/windows do not make indoor use safe.

record.title: 12VAC5-630-220 Permits and inspection statement
record.finding: Private well construction, alteration, deepening and abandonment generally require written permission. Wells must meet applicable requirements and generally require an inspection statement before operation. Stated exceptions must be evaluated, not inferred from DIY or emergency intent.

record.title: How Do Hydrologists Locate Groundwater?
record.finding: Groundwater occupies pores and fractures in soil and rock. Maps, existing well records, geologic analysis, aquifer tests and chemical analysis inform location, quantity and quality. Valleys and vegetation can be clues, not guarantees of usable water.

record.title: 12VAC5-630-410 Construction; general
record.finding: Formation and well classification determine bore, casing, screen, filter pack and grouting. These are sanitary and structural systems, not simply permeable masonry walls. Source material does not demonstrate compliance with class-specific completion requirements.

record.title: Water Dowsing
record.locator: What does science say about dowsing?
record.finding: Apparent success can reflect widespread groundwater. Scientific determination of depth, quantity and quality needs hydrologic, geologic and geophysical investigation, not reliance on rods.

record.title: Trenching and Excavation
record.finding: Excavation collapse is a major fatal hazard requiring protective systems such as appropriate sloping, shoring or shielding and competent assessment. This occupational guidance is safety evidence, not a determination that every homeowner activity has identical regulatory coverage or that it fully specifies shaft/confined-space safety.

record.title: Personal Hygiene During an Emergency
record.finding: Wash with soap and safe water; when unavailable use at least 60% alcohol sanitizer, with limits for dirty/greasy hands and chemicals. Keep wounds clean and covered, avoid contaminated water and seek care for redness, swelling or oozing. This does not validate herbal wound remedies, surgery or instrument sterilization.

record.publisher: Washington State University Extension, hosted by UC ANR
record.title: Storing Vegetables and Fruits at Home, EB1326E
record.finding: Storage depends on crop-specific temperature, humidity and ventilation. Handle produce gently, discard damaged/decaying material and separate incompatible produce. Apples can cause potatoes to sprout and carrots to become bitter. Preparation, curing and shelf life vary by crop, so one warm/dry curing rule is inadequate.

record.title: Consumer Guide to Passive Solar Home Design
record.finding: Climate-appropriate glazing, absorbers, thermal mass, heat distribution and controls work together. Masonry stores heat and can release it later; summer shading helps control gains. Orientation or mass alone does not establish a complete safe retrofit or guaranteed comfort.

record.publisher: Pacific Northwest National Laboratory / DOE Building America
record.title: Evaporative Cooling Systems
record.finding: Evaporative cooling is suited to dry climates and requires evaluation of wet-bulb conditions, airflow, capacity, maintenance and commissioning. Direct evaporation cools while adding moisture. This evidence does not validate the book's wet solar-chimney design or a Virginia humid-weather performance guarantee.

record.title: Best Wood-Burning Practices
record.finding: Check firewood moisture below 20%, store off ground with top covered and sides ventilated, maintain appliances and clear combustibles. Burn only suitable fuel and protect against smoke/CO. EPA labels this Burn Wise content a historical record, no longer updated after October 30, 2025; it is not a current local installation code or permit.

record.title: 1910.23 Ladders
record.finding: Ladders are used only for their designed purposes and within maximum intended loads. This does not establish that an ordinary ladder is a rated hoisting frame. Occupational requirements are used as safety evidence, not blanket legal advice for homeowners.

record.title: 1926.251 Rigging equipment for material handling
record.finding: Inspect lifting gear; use legible manufacturer safe-working-load identification and stay within ratings. Custom lifting accessories need appropriate design and proof testing under applicable standards. A tie-down strap, tree branch or improvised frame is not proven suitable by appearance alone.

record.title: 12VAC5-610-980 Types of privies and toilets
record.finding: The cited composting-toilet provisions require NSF Standard 41 certification and direct that removed material be buried, not placed in vegetable gardens or on the ground surface. Privy utilization, other wastewater and approvals also matter. A DIY bucket is not automatically equivalent to a compliant composting toilet; ask VDH about the applicable approved system.

record.title: Colloidal Silver: What You Need To Know
record.finding: Ingested colloidal silver can cause permanent argyria and interfere with drug absorption, with other possible harms. This source is a health-risk constraint, not validation or evaluation of a particular certified silver-containing water-treatment product.

record.title: Safe Use of Complementary Health Products and Practices
record.finding: Herbal and other supplements can have uncertain safety, drug interactions and contamination. Natural origin is not proof of efficacy or safety. This evidence does not assess the book's individual herbs, poultices or steam treatment.

record.title: 10.1-1142 Regulating the burning of woods and brush
record.finding: State law regulates open-air fires near woodland/flammable materials, including seasonal restrictions and precautions with exceptions. Check actual locality and current conditions; daylight smoke-signaling advice is not permission to burn.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: Ensuring Safe Canned Foods
record.finding: Low-acid foods require an appropriate tested pressure-canning process; a general pasteurization temperature is insufficient.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: Using Pressure Canners
record.finding: Venting, pressure, timing, altitude and natural cooling are essential controls; pressure loss requires restarting the full processing time.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: Sterilization of Empty Jars
record.finding: Presterilization, when required, uses boiling water with elevation adjustment; 158 F is not the stated jar-sterilization method.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: Cooling Jars and Testing Jar Seals
record.finding: Cool 12-24 hours, test seals, and use a new lid and the appropriate full process for eligible reprocessing within 24 hours.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: Equipment and Methods Not Recommended
record.finding: Oven canning and dry canning are not recommended science-based home-canning methods.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: General Information on Pickling
record.finding: Use tested food, water and vinegar proportions and specified acidity and storage; fermentation salt is a safety control.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: Pickled Eggs
record.finding: There are no recommended home-canning directions for pickled eggs. Keep them refrigerated; room-temperature storage has caused botulism.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: Sauerkraut
record.finding: This tested method specifies cabbage weight, salt, temperature, fermentation duration and subsequent refrigerated or processed storage.

record.title: Vegetable Fermentation
record.locator: Fermentation components: salt, temperature, and storage
record.finding: Salt concentration and temperature affect fermentation. Measure carefully and follow a tested recipe specific to the vegetable.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: Sun Drying
record.finding: Outdoor drying is appropriate for selected fruits under suitable conditions; meats and most vegetables need controlled drying.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / University of Georgia
record.title: Jerky
record.locator: Handling, meat preparation, heating, drying and storage
record.finding: Refrigerate marination, trim fat, control strip thickness, and follow a heating/drying method. Its room-temperature storage guidance is two weeks, not an unspecified number of months.

record.title: Cook to a Safe Minimum Internal Temperature
record.finding: Use a food thermometer and the food-specific internal temperature and any required rest. Cooking guidance does not establish shelf stability.

record.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
record.title: How long after smoking meat should it be refrigerated?
record.locator: Primary-source search-indexed article text; direct open timed out
record.finding: The accessible USDA article excerpt directs refrigeration within two hours after smoking and use within four days or freezing. Only that excerpt was reviewed.

record.title: 7 Factors That Prolong Your Food Storage Supply
record.locator: Moisture, container, and botulism warning paragraphs
record.finding: Oxygen-reduced packages with moist food can support botulism; the source specifies about 10% or less moisture for this dry-food packaging context.

record.publisher: Washington State University Extension, hosted by University of California ANR
record.title: Storing Vegetables and Fruits at Home, EB1326E
record.locator: PDF pp. 2-10; storage conditions, separation and crop tables
record.finding: Success depends on crop, temperature, humidity and ventilation. Separate apples from potatoes and carrots; published storage durations are conditional estimates.

record.title: Food Storage Guidelines for Consumers
record.locator: Dates, refrigeration, FIFO and product tables; revised October 2025
record.finding: Most date labels address quality. Monitor refrigerated food below 40 F, freezer at 0 F, and use appropriate product-specific storage and rotation.

record.title: Home-Canned Foods
record.locator: Key points, safe canning, and toxin warning
record.finding: Botulinum toxin cannot be detected by sight, smell or taste. Use safe methods; do not taste suspect food.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: Storing Home Canned Foods
record.finding: Label and date properly processed jars; store cool, dark and dry. Best-quality guidance is generally to can the amount used within a year.

record.title: Types of Food Ingredients
record.finding: Preservatives include antimicrobials and antioxidants, rather than serving only cosmetic roles; ingredients must meet the same safety standard regardless of origin.

record.title: How GMOs Are Regulated in the United States
record.locator: Agency roles and FDA consultation sections
record.finding: FDA, EPA and USDA have defined regulatory roles; the source's blanket claim of no meaningful safety assessment is not supported.

record.title: Harvesting and storing melons, squash and pumpkins
record.locator: Winter squash and pumpkins; reviewed in 2026
record.finding: The source gives around 50-55 F and 50% relative humidity for winter squash and pumpkins, with variety-dependent keeping time.

record.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service
record.title: What is freezer burn?
record.locator: Primary-source search-indexed article text; direct open timed out
record.finding: The accessible article excerpt distinguishes drying and quality loss from food becoming unsafe; heavy freezer burn may warrant discarding for quality. Only the indexed excerpt was reviewed.

record.title: Investigation of Illnesses: Morel Mushrooms (May 2023)
record.finding: Qualified expert identification is important. This source directly addresses mushrooms, not every plant; applying caution to plant shortcuts is reviewer risk analysis.

record.title: Storing Up for Winter with Forageables
record.finding: The official Virginia article supports positive identification, minimizing damage and obtaining permission. It also discusses seasonal food and acorn leaching; its older WMA-law summary is not treated as a current permit.

record.publisher: NIH National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health
record.title: Dandelion
record.finding: No compelling scientific evidence supports dandelion for a health condition. Food use and medicinal dosing differ; interactions and safety uncertainty remain.

record.publisher: NIH National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health
record.title: Red Clover
record.finding: Menopause and bone-density results are inconsistent; supplement safety in pregnancy/breastfeeding is a concern. This is not evidence about every Trifolium species.

record.title: Morel and other wild-mushroom recommendations
record.finding: Cooking cannot guarantee safety; false-morel toxins may remain after heating. Expert identification and appropriate storage are necessary. Same page as W01, a separately scoped evidence locator, not an independent source.

record.title: Preventing Rat Lungworm
record.finding: Do not eat raw or undercooked snails/slugs in affected areas. Wash raw vegetables thoroughly. This does not certify purging, an insect recipe or Virginia prevalence.

record.title: Venomous Snakes at Work
record.finding: Prompt medical care is needed; do not use folk therapies. Plantain poultice/juice is not supported as snakebite treatment.

record.title: 4VAC5-30-50. Flowers, plants, minerals, etc.
record.locator: Current rule text, including personal edible-collection exception
record.finding: The rule generally protects vegetation but expressly permits personal or individual gathering of edible fruits, berries, fungi and nuts. This does not authorize digging roots, stripping bark or tapping; site scope still matters.

record.title: Plantago major
record.finding: The profile describes flowering stems under twelve inches, contradicting the book's seven-to-twenty-foot description. The source does not validate medicinal uses or identify a specimen.

record.title: Prunus virginiana
record.finding: Stems, leaves and seeds have cyanogenic hazards. The book's human-use bark claims cannot be treated as safe doses or the warning restricted to livestock.

record.title: Cassava and bamboo shoots
record.finding: Only selected bamboo species are used as food; cyanogenic shoots require appropriate preparation and discarded cooking water. Commercial canned-product reassurance does not validate arbitrary home canning.

record.title: Homemade maple syrup
record.locator: Tapping, sap yield and evaporation instructions
record.finding: Proper taps and food-grade collection are described. Syrup concentrates sap by evaporation to a controlled endpoint; adding thirty-five parts water is not this process.

record.title: Salicis cortex
record.finding: Defined willow-bark preparations have restrictions, salicylate interactions and gastrointestinal adverse effects; childbirth leaf chewing is not validated by this monograph.

record.title: Healthy Gardening Practices to Reduce Exposure to Lead-Contaminated Soil
record.locator: Soil testing, siting and produce preparation
record.finding: Assess actual contamination and avoid sources; soil testing and exposure controls matter. This is not evidence for a universal one-hundred-foot boundary or uphill safety.

record.title: Food Allergies: What You Need to Know
record.finding: Food allergy can be serious; a mild reaction does not establish a mild allergy. A taste is not an identification or allergy-clearance procedure.

record.title: Complementary and Alternative Medicine
record.finding: No food or herb combination is proven to slow, cure or prevent recurrence of cancer. Clinical care must not be replaced with this book's cancer claims.

record.publisher: NIH National Library of Medicine / MedlinePlus
record.title: Poisoning first aid
record.finding: Do not wait for symptoms in suspected poisoning; seek poison-control or emergency guidance. This is not support for a daylily antidote or other herbal treatment.

record.title: What You Should Know about Eye Drops
record.finding: Drugs used in eyes must be sterile. A homemade rose infusion is not an established sterile treatment for eye infection.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation
record.title: How Do I Preserve Foods?
record.finding: Food preservation needs food- and process-specific instructions; broad drying, fermentation or oil-extraction statements are not complete validated methods.

record.title: Urgent Maternal Warning Signs and Symptoms
record.locator: Key points, heavy bleeding after pregnancy, chest/heart warning signs
record.finding: Heavy postpartum bleeding and listed serious maternal symptoms warrant immediate medical care, rather than an unvalidated pollen or willow preparation.

record.title: An essential guide to building an emergency fund
record.locator: Savings habit, amount, cash flow and safe accessible storage
record.finding: Emergency reserves and feasible saving help with shocks; target and location depend on circumstances. It does not recommend a universal six-month-income target or loan plan.

record.title: Understanding Deposit Insurance
record.locator: Official primary-source search excerpt; direct HTML and brochure access returned 403
record.finding: Indexed FDIC text states 250000 dollars per depositor per insured bank per ownership category. Only that primary excerpt was reviewed; it does not support a verified record.

record.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
record.title: Asset Allocation and Diversification
record.locator: Allocation, horizon, risk tolerance and diversification
record.finding: Allocation depends on the investor's horizon and risk tolerance. Diversification addresses concentration, not a guaranteed return or universal ranking of asset classes.

record.publisher: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission / Investor.gov
record.title: Mutual Funds
record.locator: Fees, risks, index and actively managed fund sections
record.finding: Funds differ in risks, objectives and expenses; all involve risk, but the category cannot be dismissed as uniformly disappointing or called insured/safe.

record.title: Multi-Level Marketing Businesses and Pyramid Schemes
record.finding: Most legitimate-MLM participants make little or no money; some lose money. Pressure, recruitment incentives, costs and earnings claims warrant investigation.

record.title: Topic no. 420, Bartering income
record.locator: Reporting barter income and estimated tax
record.finding: Include fair market value of goods/services received as applicable gross income; business reporting and estimated-tax obligations may apply. A cashless exchange is not inherently tax-free.

record.publisher: Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services
record.title: Virginia's Home Kitchen Food Processing Exemptions
record.locator: July 2024 guidance, food categories, labels and restrictions; linked by current VDACS kitchen-business page
record.finding: Some defined low-risk foods and specified products have conditional inspection exemptions. Food category, labeling and sales restrictions still matter; not every preserve or sauce is exempt.

record.title: Food Storage Guidelines for Consumers
record.locator: Revised October 2025; dates, product tables and storage
record.finding: Most dates describe quality, with infant formula an exception. Product type, opening, temperature and packaging govern storage; the guide does not support lifelong keeping of all listed foods.

record.title: Seed for the Garden
record.locator: Saved-seed storage, testing and vegetable viability table
record.finding: Seed longevity differs by crop and storage. Common vegetable averages are measured in years, and germination testing is advised; ordinary stored seed is not a guaranteed hundred-year supply.

record.title: How to Create an Emergency Water Supply
record.finding: CDC recommends suitable food-grade containers and replacing home-filled stored water every six months; follow bottled-water labeling. No worry-free multi-year blanket promise follows.

record.title: Sunscreen: How to Help Protect Your Skin from the Sun
record.finding: SPF requires finished-product testing. A homemade zinc-oxide mix has no established protection from ingredient presence alone; use appropriate labeled sun protection.

record.title: Regulation of Skin-Applied Repellents
record.finding: Registration includes safety and efficacy evaluation for labeled use; exempt essential-oil products have not necessarily been evaluated for effectiveness. This is not a tested recipe for the book's mixture.

record.title: Selecting and Serving Produce Safely
record.finding: Wash produce under running water. Washing reduces but does not eliminate contamination; household detergents and commercial produce washes are not recommended substitutes.

record.title: About Fluoride
record.finding: Fluoride helps prevent cavities; twice-daily brushing with appropriate fluoride toothpaste is recommended. Baking soda, oil and fragrance do not establish an equivalent anticaries product.

record.title: Home-prepared Diets
record.finding: A board-certified veterinary nutrition consultation and exact balanced formulation are recommended. A short list of meat, grains and vegetables does not establish nutritional completeness.

record.title: Top tips for a safe spring cleaning
record.locator: Labels, mixtures, ventilation, storage and ingredient classes
record.finding: Follow cleaner labels, avoid unassessed mixtures and protect against skin/eye and inhalation hazards. This is general safety evidence, not a test of each book recipe.

record.title: My child got into the baking soda: Risks and treatment
record.locator: Acid reaction and carbon dioxide explanation
record.finding: Bicarbonate plus acid releases carbon dioxide. Applying that chemistry to the book's closed spray bottle identifies an unassessed pressure risk, not a tested prediction of bottle failure.

record.title: Don't Be Tempted to Use Expired Medicines
record.finding: Expired drugs may be ineffective or harmful; follow expiry and storage guidance. This does not establish a shelf life for every bandage or device.

record.title: Know When and How to Use Antibiotics, and When to Skip Them
record.finding: Antibiotics need an appropriate diagnosis and directed use; misuse/overuse contributes to resistance. Their presence in a stockpile is not permission for unsupervised treatment or trade.

record.title: The Great Depression
record.locator: Banking panics, policy, contraction and recovery
record.finding: The history is more complex than one crash or household cash-holding choice; real/nominal rates and policy matter. It does not establish the book's global count, exact wealth stories or a new depression forecast.

record.title: The Great Recession and Its Aftermath
record.finding: The Federal Reserve provided monetary accommodation during the downturn; recession does not mechanically force all interest rates upward. Individual loan terms still matter.

record.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History
record.title: Plastic Payments
record.locator: Official indexed primary-source excerpt; direct page opens failed
record.finding: Indexed museum text places Diners' Club in 1950 and general-purpose bank/plastic cards in the late 1950s. Earlier merchant credit existed, so the correction concerns modern general-purpose cards, not all credit.

record.title: Natural Toxins in Food
record.finding: Raw or undercooked kidney beans can contain hazardous lectin; appropriate cooking is necessary. A generic slow-cooker suggestion is not a validated bean preparation.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / USDA
record.title: Ensuring Safe Canned Foods
record.finding: Food-specific tested processing is necessary, especially pressure canning low-acid foods. A seal, vacuum or simplified all-bacteria-killed account cannot validate every product.

record.publisher: NIH National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health
record.title: Colds, Flu, and Complementary Health Approaches
record.finding: Evidence and safety depend on the ingredient and use. This page does not establish efficacy, dose or refrigerated life for the book's particular missing-ginger formula.

record.title: Protect operational technology against activity targeting PLCs
record.locator: July 30, 2026 bulletin; exposure warning and defensive mitigations
record.finding: CISA describes risks from publicly exposed OT and advises protected remote access, password protection and exposure reduction. This bulletin concerns water-sector PLCs; it does not investigate the freezer incidents.

record.title: SP 800-161 Rev. 1, updated 2024: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices
record.locator: CSRC publication abstract and revision metadata; not a review of the full manual
record.finding: The abstract directly supports identifying, assessing and mitigating cybersecurity risks in acquired products and services. It does not verify a particular provider, DLA policy or incident.

record.title: SP 800-82 Rev. 3: Guide to Operational Technology Security
record.locator: Publication abstract and metadata; not a review of the full manual
record.finding: OT security must account for physical-system performance, reliability and safety. Revision 3 remains the final publication shown; the page identifies Revision 4 as an initial public draft.

record.title: Personal data security incident involving a third-party service provider
record.locator: October 30, 2026 notice; affected records, fields, payment qualifier and operating status
record.finding: Cathay reports approximately 53000 affected bookings, mostly names, flights and references, with additional possible fields for a subset. It reports no evidence of financial/payment access and no effect on its own operations. These are company statements, not an independent forensic audit.

record.title: Orange Cyberdefense becomes Mistral AI European MSSP design partner
record.locator: October 29, 2026 announcement; early access, use cases, oversight and European infrastructure
record.finding: The company announces early access to a Mistral Large 4 cybersecurity variant, gradual operational integration, European computing and human oversight. Planned benefits do not establish achieved results or universal necessity.

record.title: Military freezer malfunctions treated as suspected cyberattack
record.locator: October 29, 2026 original Reuters reporting by Raphael Satter, AJ Vicens and Phil Stewart; opening and French-freezer discussion
record.finding: Reports suspected hacking, at least six commissaries, late-August timing and a Fort Huachuca notice on August 26. French losses include an estimate. The article does not establish the U.S. controller brand or a common exploit. Original journalism provides attributed incident context, not official forensic confirmation.

record.title: Keep Food Safe After a Disaster or Emergency
record.finding: Appliance thermometers, refrigerator at or below 40 F, freezer at or below 0 F, closed-door 4/48/24-hour outage estimates, cold-source planning and no tasting to establish safety.

record.title: Emergencies: Food safety in Virginia
record.locator: Power-outage preparation, during and after an emergency
record.finding: Virginia reinforces thermometer use, closed-door outage estimates, ice/cooler planning, maintaining 40 F or below and discarding questionable food.

record.title: Food and Water Safety During Power Outages and Floods
record.locator: Before power emergencies and determining food safety after restoration
record.finding: FDA recommends appliance thermometers and warns that appearance/odor cannot establish safety and that thorough cooking may not make temperature-abused perishables safe. This examination does not adopt the page as an industrial cold-chain contract standard.

record.title: Food Safety During Power Outage
record.locator: Refrigerated and frozen item-specific tables, reviewed August 8, 2024
record.finding: The tables distinguish discard decisions after more than two hours at 40 F or above, category-specific exceptions and refreezing conditions. Ice cream and frozen yogurt are discarded even in the ice-crystal column. The outage estimates do not describe active heating or certify previously warmed food.

record.title: Subsistence Home
record.locator: Official-domain search excerpt; direct page returned HTTP 403
record.finding: The official excerpt identifies DLA as DoD Executive Agent for Subsistence. It does not verify the supplied office-code pairs, affected inventory ownership, contract clauses or incident losses.

record.title: DoorDash to Acquire Instacart to Help Local Stores Win
record.locator: October 29, 2026 definitive agreement; equity value and closing conditions
record.finding: The announcement gives approximately 17 billion dollars in equity value for a proposed acquisition, with closing expected in late 2027 or the first half of 2028 subject to conditions; it does not announce completed ownership.

record.title: ADT to be Acquired by Thrive Holdings
record.locator: October 29, 2026 agreement announcement; value definitions and completion qualifier
record.finding: ADT announces a proposed transaction with approximately 7.6 billion dollars equity value and 15.3 billion enterprise value. Going private is contingent on completion; the two values measure different things.

record.title: Polymarket status page
record.locator: Live component availability on access date; no historical loss figures in retrieved content
record.finding: The retrieved page shows present operational status, not proof of the supplied 2.6-million-dollar loss estimate or the historical attack mechanism. It is contextual evidence only.

record.title: How to Make Water Safe in an Emergency
record.locator: Boiling, disinfecting, filtering and chemical-contamination sections
record.finding: Turbidity removal is distinct from germ control; follow appropriate treatment and safe storage. Boiling/disinfection cannot make fuel/toxic-chemical contamination safe.

record.title: Emergency Disinfection of Drinking Water
record.finding: Filtration/settling before disinfection is not complete treatment. Boiling/disinfection does not remove metals, salts and many chemicals. No improvised filter or still in this book is certified.

record.title: Collecting Rainwater and Your Health
record.locator: Contamination, first flush, screened openings, testing and treatment
record.finding: Screens help exclude bugs/debris; roof, plumbing and storage can introduce hazards. Intended use, contaminant-specific treatment and testing matter.

record.title: Rainwater Harvesting
record.locator: Rain-barrel exclusion, supply continuity and intended uses
record.finding: VDH distinguishes qualifying rain barrels from regulated systems and notes drought/continuity needs. Do not assume a generic connected barrel or potable system qualifies for an exclusion.

record.title: Groundwater Wells
record.locator: Official search excerpt on pumping and pump-intake water level; direct retrieval timed out
record.finding: Pumping changes water level and a pump can take air when water drops below its intake. This does not validate the book's pump geometry, lift or sanitary installation.

record.title: Vegetable Gardening in Containers
record.locator: Containers, media and watering; revised March 2026
record.finding: Suitable container size, clean prior use, drainage holes, porous media and moisture monitoring are important. The publication does not establish the book's harvest or year-round food guarantees.

record.title: Seed For The Garden
record.locator: Saved and purchased seed storage, labeling, germination and viability table
record.finding: Cool/dry storage and labels are supported. Crop-dependent viability and germination checks contradict a universal guarantee; the source does not validate unspecified oven heat or rice as an oxygen absorber.

record.publisher: National Center for Home Food Preservation / University of Georgia
record.title: Sun Drying
record.locator: Opening food categories and outdoor drying conditions
record.finding: Most vegetables and meats are not recommended for outdoor drying; controlled conditions matter. A homemade solar enclosure has not been demonstrated to meet a food-specific process.

record.title: Raw Milk Questions and Answers
record.finding: Raw milk can contain pathogens; appropriate pasteurization reduces them. This is not a complete cheese recipe or proof that unspecified aging controls establish safety.

record.title: Safe Minimum Internal Temperatures
record.locator: Food thermometer and food-specific endpoint/rest chart
record.finding: Measure food-core temperature with a suitable thermometer. A hot cooker surface, reflective design or subjective cooked appearance does not validate the book's solar processes.

record.title: Small Wind Guidebook
record.locator: Generator mechanism, balance of system, stand-alone battery charging and siting
record.finding: Wind electricity requires an actual mechanical/electrical conversion system, suitable balance of system and safe installation. Battery charging needs appropriate control; a diode is not a complete charging system.

record.title: Guide to Passive Solar Home Design
record.locator: Two-page guide, elements of passive design
record.finding: Proper orientation, glazing, storage mass, distribution and seasonal control work together. These principles do not certify a building assembly or the book's untested heater/cooker designs.

record.title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning: Protect Your Family and Yourself
record.locator: Fuel-fired sources, safe installation/flues and prevention
record.finding: Improperly installed or vented fuel-burning equipment can produce dangerous CO. Room ventilation does not certify an improvised indoor heater; suitable installation and alarms matter.

record.title: 12VAC5-610-980 Types of privies
record.finding: The provision requires composting-toilet certification to current NSF Standard 41 and prescribed disposal, including burial and no vegetable-garden or ground-surface application. The bucket outline is not certified by elapsed months.

record.title: How to Create and Maintain an Indoor Worm Composting Bin
record.locator: Worm species, bedding, food selection and covering scraps
record.finding: Use appropriate worms and moist bedding with suitable feedstocks and covered scraps. Avoid animal by-products and invasive worm species; this is not a human-waste or mixed-garbage treatment certification.

record.title: 9VAC25-740 Water Reclamation and Reuse Regulation
record.finding: Graywater is distinguished from treated reclaimed water and excludes toilets, kitchen/dishwasher and soiled-diaper streams. Graywater is excluded from this chapter, but other applicable rules still apply. This is not a site-specific permit determination.

record.title: Open Burning
record.locator: Official-domain search excerpt; direct retrieval returned HTTP 403
record.finding: Virginia guidance rejects tire/hazardous-material burning. A homemade signal is not an authorization to burn tires; local and current fire restrictions still need checking.

record.title: Furbearer Trapping Regulations and Seasons
record.locator: General trapping regulations, methods and ethical responsibilities
record.finding: Permissions, species, seasons, methods, checks and non-target risks matter. No improvised pointed trap or spear/sling hunting method is approved by this examination.

record.title: NOAA Weather Radio Receivers
record.finding: NOAA weather broadcasts use seven VHF channels from 162.400 to 162.550 MHz and cannot be received on a simple AM/FM receiver. No transmitter or weather-band capability is established by the book's circuit.

record.publisher: National Capital Poison Center / Poison Control
record.title: Is it safe to make soap at home?
record.locator: Lye risks, protective equipment, essential oils and safer alternatives
record.finding: Lye causes corrosive skin/eye injuries and calls for appropriate PPE and controlled handling. Finished formulation and exposure matter; oils and fragrances are not universally safe. The book's missing formula is not validated.

record.title: Oral Health Tips for Adults
record.finding: CDC recommends brushing with fluoride toothpaste and regular oral hygiene. The homemade fluoride-free products are not established clinical equivalents or validated storage formulations.

record.title: Make a First Aid Kit: What to Include
record.locator: Kit contents, personal medications and regular expiration/replacement checks
record.finding: A kit should suit actual needs and be checked regularly with used/outdated contents replaced. This is not approval of vinegar wipes, food-based treatments or herbal medicine substitutions.

record.title: Chamomile: Usefulness and Safety
record.finding: Evidence for particular products/conditions is limited; combination-product results do not establish chamomile alone. No windowsill preparation or dose is validated.

record.title: Lavender: Usefulness and Safety
record.finding: Some product-specific preliminary research exists, but quality and formulation limitations prevent treating a home-grown plant as a validated headache or anxiety medicine.

record.title: Peppermint Oil: Usefulness and Safety
record.locator: Leaf evidence versus oil-product research and adverse effects
record.finding: Limited evidence for particular enteric-coated oil products does not establish medicinal benefit of peppermint leaf, arbitrary oil drops or the book's oral products. Side effects can occur.

record.publisher: Virginia Department of Housing and Community Development
record.title: Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code
record.finding: Buildings and structures must meet applicable code, enforced locally. The source is not an engineering approval, a site-specific permit ruling or a load assessment of these shelters, cellars or trailers.

record.title: Boating Equipment Regulations
record.locator: Wearable life jackets, paddlecraft and required-equipment overview
record.finding: Appropriately sized approved life jackets and relevant equipment are required for applicable vessels. A shallow test does not certify the book's watercraft construction or capacity.

record.title: Can the use of fragrances indoors cause health impacts?
record.finding: Fragrances can affect sensitive people. Pleasant odor or natural origin does not prove air purification, universal safety or a therapeutic outcome.

record.title: Why Drive White LEDs with Constant Current?
record.finding: Bare white LEDs need current management compatible with ratings; voltage alone can produce widely varying current. This does not specify the book's LED package, generator or a complete flashlight design.

record.title: Container and Raised-Bed Gardening
record.locator: Containers and plants: drainage and matching cultural needs
record.finding: Drainage holes and appropriate growing media matter; gravel/stones are not needed at a container bottom. Match plant light/water needs rather than assuming one mixed herb planter suits all.

record.title: Mercury Thermometers
record.locator: Fever thermometers, alternatives and spill/disposal guidance
record.finding: Mercury thermometers are actual measuring instruments with a scale and breakage/spill hazards, not a makeshift measurement method. Safer mercury-free options exist; replacement choice does not validate the book's improvised medical supplies.

record.title: Aquaponics
record.locator: Water quality, bacteria/biofiltration and species considerations
record.finding: Aquaponics depends on a balanced managed system of fish, plants and bacteria with water-quality and oxygen control. This does not validate an undriven water wheel or promise powerless year-round food production.

record.title: Emergency water supply
record.locator: Water amounts, containers, cleaning and rotation
record.support_scope: At least one US gallon per person daily for three days; try two weeks. Suitable containers and six-month home-filled-water replacement. Extra needs can increase quantities.

record.title: Making water safe
record.support_scope: Safe water sources, clarification versus germ treatment, and limits for fuel/toxic-chemical contamination. CDC boiling elevation boundary is 6500 feet.

record.title: Emergency disinfection of drinking water
record.support_scope: One-minute rolling boil; three minutes above 5000 feet. Boiling/disinfection does not remove salts, metals and many chemicals. Metric altitude parenthetical on the page is inconsistent; this core uses feet only.

record.title: Testing well water
record.locator: Test panel, certified laboratory and health department advice
record.support_scope: Testing and interpretation depend on local hazards. A test panel does not establish pump availability, plumbing compliance or a permanent safety guarantee.

record.title: Food safety after an emergency
record.locator: Preparation, closed-door outage estimates and discard guidance
record.support_scope: Thermometers and cold-source planning; refrigerator/freezer 4/48/24-hour estimates under the stated outage conditions; unsafe food may appear normal.

record.title: Food safety during power outage
record.support_scope: Food-specific discard/refreeze decisions and exceptions. Ice cream/frozen yogurt are discard entries even in the ice-crystal column; generic rules must not erase exceptions.

record.title: Survival kit supplies
record.support_scope: Three-day evacuation and two-week home supplies, easy-to-prepare food, sanitation supplies and a manual opener. Product quantities and household meal planning below are editorial applications.

record.title: Power outage safety
record.support_scope: Flashlights, electrical-needs planning, medical-provider advice, alerts and relocation when home conditions or medical power cannot be maintained.

record.title: Carbon monoxide safety
record.support_scope: Portable fuel generators outdoors at least 20 feet from structures; no indoor grills/camp stoves; alarms, installation and fresh-air/medical response.

record.title: Handwashing
record.support_scope: Soap and clean running water, 20-second scrub, rinse and dry; handwashing after toilet use and before food handling.

record.title: Emergency personal hygiene
record.locator: Temporary station, sanitizer limits and bathing
record.support_scope: Jug-based handwashing, at least 60% alcohol sanitizer when soap/water unavailable, limits with dirt/chemicals and authority-specific bathing advice.

record.title: Stay connected
record.support_scope: Important numbers, at least two meeting places, out-of-town contact and multiple communication routes; texts may succeed when calls do not.

record.title: Weather radio receivers
record.support_scope: Weather broadcasts require compatible VHF reception on 162.400-162.550 MHz; a plain AM/FM radio does not provide that capability.

record.title: Food safety during emergencies
record.support_scope: Virginia corroboration for appliance thermometers, closed-door estimates, cold-source planning and no taste testing.

record.title: Sewage backups
record.locator: What to do first and prevention
record.support_scope: Stop household water use during a sewage backup; contact the responsible service. Do not flush wipes or other trash. This provider is an example source, not the household’s confirmed utility.

record.title: Drinking water advisories
record.support_scope: Follow actual advisory uses/restrictions; appliance water filters do not override a boil advisory. Do not use connected refrigerator water/ice during advisories.

record.title: Safe generator use
record.support_scope: Running/starting requirements, professional transfer equipment, no outlet backfeeding, safe rated connections and cooling before refueling. No DIY wiring procedure is supplied.

record.title: Food and water safety during power outages and floods
record.locator: Power outages: warning after restored-power discussion
record.support_scope: Inadequately refrigerated or frozen perishable food can cause illness even after thorough cooking. Used for this warning only; FoodSafety.gov item tables govern this core’s food decisions, not the FDA page’s broader temperature statements.

record.title: Bleach treatment
record.guidance: Use the concentration-specific EPA table; for clear water use eight drops of 6% or six of 8.25% bleach per gallon. Double for cloudy, colored or very cold water after settling/prefiltration; wait 30 minutes. If no slight chlorine odor, repeat dose and wait 15 more minutes. Do not infer precise milliliters from an arbitrary dropper.

record.title: Calcium hypochlorite
record.guidance: EPA describes a heaping teaspoon of high-test calcium hypochlorite in two gallons to make stock, then one part stock to 100 parts water (one pint per 12.5 gallons). Follow product suitability and oxidizer precautions; do not adopt the book’s inconsistent ounce-per-three-quarts shortcut.

record.title: Iodine limits
record.guidance: Use only a defined product and label protocol. CDC cautions against iodine for pregnancy, thyroid conditions or iodine hypersensitivity and use beyond a few weeks. Do not rely on iodine for all parasites; it is not the default household long-term treatment.

record.title: Emergency boiling
record.guidance: Use CDC’s rolling boil: one minute, or three minutes above 6,500 feet, then cool and protect from recontamination. This controls germs and does not remove chemical hazards. EPA’s displayed altitude threshold differs (5,000 feet and an inconsistent metric equivalent); this dataset explicitly adopts CDC’s threshold, with local health instructions taking precedence.

record.title: Container sanitation and storage
record.guidance: Use CDC’s wash/sanitize/fill/close method and six-month replacement interval for home-filled water. A sealed lid and one bleach dose do not establish indefinite safe storage. Keep container sanitation solution separate from drinking-water dosing.

record.title: Pools are nonpotable reserves
record.guidance: Use pool water only for appropriate non-drinking purposes; normal pool maintenance does not make a drinking-water supply.

record.title: Rainfall arithmetic and reliability
record.guidance: US liquid gallon is 231 cubic inches: gallons = horizontal square feet × rainfall inches × 144 / 231. Thus 850 × 23 gives 12,187.012987 gallons/year, 33.389077/day gross; 2,000 × 23 gives 28,675.324675/year. The book’s 6,452-gallon reference is inconsistent. Subtract first flush, collection losses and overflow and model dry periods; annual yield divided by 365 is not dependable daily supply.

record.title: Virginia rainwater law
record.guidance: Virginia allows potable rainwater under Tier 4 requirements. Check system applicability, construction and operation permits, testing and building/local requirements. The reviewed design rule requires first flush but does not state four inches; the claimed general tax credit was not substantiated and remains unresolved.

record.title: Well sanitary completion
record.guidance: Use an approved class-specific casing, screen, grout and wellhead design; a buried plastic bag and tamped mud do not establish sanitary protection. Required testing and inspection still apply.

record.title: Dowsing
record.guidance: Use hydrogeologic investigation and testing. Do not rely on crossing rods to establish groundwater depth, quantity or quality.

record.title: Relative humidity
record.guidance: At fixed vapor content, warming lowers relative humidity and cooling raises it. Dew requires an adequately cold surface; fog interception is a separate mechanism. Neither high relative humidity alone nor morning sunlight establishes harvest yield.

record.title: Greywater controls
record.guidance: Treat greywater as potentially contaminated. Use approved separate systems and use-specific treatment, bypass and backflow protections; Virginia’s cited residential provisions limit untreated tank storage to 24 hours. Do not use untreated shower water for dishes or treat any outdoor discharge as automatically lawful.

record.title: Potable reuse
record.guidance: Potable reuse needs purpose-designed treatment, monitoring and applicable approvals. Conventional wastewater effluent and household distilled urine are not established safe drinking-water sources by these descriptions.

record.title: Food during a power outage
record.guidance: Keep refrigerator/freezer doors closed, monitor time and temperature, and follow CDC discard guidance. An unopened refrigerator normally gives four hours; full and half-full freezers approximately 48 and 24 hours respectively. Do not taste food for safety or preserve food that has become unsafe.

record.title: Water treatment and chemical limits
record.guidance: Use CDC rolling-boil guidance: one minute, or three above 6500 feet, then cool and protect. Boiling and disinfection do not remove toxic chemicals. Match any disinfectant to product, concentration, water condition and label contact time. CDC and EPA currently display different high-altitude thresholds; this examination explicitly uses CDC. No generic filter or silver additive is endorsed.

record.title: Stored safe water
record.guidance: Use safe water and sanitized suitable food-grade containers; keep closed, cool, shaded and dated. CDC recommends replacing home-filled water every six months. Container sanitation solution and drinking-water dosing are different procedures.

record.title: Combustion indoors
record.guidance: CO is invisible and odorless. Outdoor-only stoves, lanterns, grills and generators must not become indoor appliances merely because a window is open. Generators belong outdoors more than 20 feet from openings. Use correctly installed vented equipment and battery-backed CO alarms. Never heat a home with a gas oven.

record.title: Medical claims
record.guidance: Keep wounds clean with soap and safe water and covered; obtain urgent assessment for infection or serious injury. Historical honey, herbs, alcohol, steam and surgical-tool lists are not validated treatments or sterile procedures. This examination does not supply diagnoses, dosing or DIY surgery instructions.

record.title: Rated lifting equipment
record.guidance: Use ladders only for designed purposes and lifting gear within its identified working-load ratings. A ladder, tie-down strap, improvised tripod or tree branch is not an approved hoist simply because it appears sturdy. OSHA sources provide safety constraints; applicability to a particular homeowner operation is not determined.

record.title: Stew must not use the book’s water-bath process
record.guidance: Reject the page 43-45 stew process. Low-acid combinations require an appropriate tested pressure-canning recipe and all ingredient, jar, altitude and canner controls. NCHFP soup guidance excludes thickeners, dairy, rice and pasta. A vacuum seal does not prove safe processing; do not improvise a pressure-canning substitution for arbitrary stew.

record.title: Unsafe raw-meat sun drying
record.guidance: Reject uncontrolled multi-day raw-meat drying and brittle texture as proof of safety. Use a validated jerky process with controlled meat handling, heating and drying; NCHFP gives a 160 F internal-temperature control and specific methods. No blanket shelf-life or parasite-kill promise is adopted.

record.title: Pickles need a tested recipe
record.guidance: Use tested food/vinegar/water proportions, specified acidity and processing/storage directions. Do not dilute vinegar arbitrarily or assume hot filling followed by room-temperature storage is safe. Fermented products also require controlled salt and conditions.

record.title: Rainwater is not automatically potable
record.guidance: Test and treat for actual microbial and chemical hazards; generic filters or boiling alone may be insufficient. Keep potable and nonpotable piping protected. Virginia potable rainwater systems require applicable construction/operation approvals, with specific rain-barrel exclusions for other systems.

record.title: Ferrocement construction not validated
record.guidance: The book supplies no structural thickness, reinforcement calculation, strength test, certified contact materials or complete potable design. Mortar ratios and one week of curing do not establish a safe tank. Obtain qualified design and suitable materials.

record.title: Silver additives not validated
record.guidance: No validated silver dose, contact time or complete water-safety protocol is provided. Do not ingest improvised colloidal-silver preparations or equate this proposal with a certified treatment device. NCCIH documents ingestion harms; it does not evaluate every silver-containing water product.

record.title: Dowsing is not a reliable well investigation
record.guidance: Use geological and hydrological investigation and water testing to establish likely depth, yield and quality. Rod movement or claimed intuition does not supply those measurements.

record.title: Well shafts require qualified protective design
record.guidance: Do not enter a hand-dug shaft using this chapter as a safety plan. Improvised timber rings, taper and masonry replacement do not establish collapse protection. Atmospheric hazards, access, rescue, rated rigging and compliant sanitary completion need independent professional assessment.

record.title: Avoid flame-based security lighting
record.guidance: Fires near windows, elevated torches and unattended perimeter flames create ignition and exposure hazards. Use safe nonflame lighting, observation, escape plans and emergency assistance.

record.title: Cooling must fit climate and airflow design
record.guidance: Direct evaporation cools by adding moisture and is most useful in dry air. The proposed solar chimney does not demonstrate a coherent cooled-supply/exhaust path, reliable draft or humid-climate comfort. Site-specific design and measurements are required; overheating needs a separate safe response plan.

record.title: Do not improvise flue distribution
record.guidance: Use the approved appliance and chimney configuration, required clearances and qualified inspection. Long or room-to-room exhaust pipes are not a generic heat exchanger; poor draft, creosote and CO can result. The EPA Burn Wise page is archived guidance, not current installation code.

record.title: Seasoning time is not a moisture measurement
record.guidance: Store suitable firewood off the ground with covered top and ventilated sides; verify moisture with a meter, below 20% in EPA guidance. Six to twelve months alone does not prove dry fuel.

record.title: Bucket waste is not approved garden compost
record.guidance: The cited Virginia rule requires NSF Standard 41 certification for composting toilets and directs removed material to burial, not vegetable gardens or ground surface. Do not assume a covered bucket, lack of odor or elapsed time provides pathogen reduction or approval. Consult VDH for applicable approved sanitation and other wastewater arrangements.

record.title: CO is not visible smoke
record.guidance: Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless. Smoke appearance cannot reveal its presence or absence; appropriate alarms, safe appliance placement and venting are needed.

record.title: Canning needs a tested process, not merely a seal
record.guidance: Reject 158 F for 20 minutes as a universal sterilization rule. Low-acid home-canned food needs an appropriate tested pressure-canning process. Follow the exact food, formulation, preparation, pack, jar, headspace, time, pressure and altitude requirements. A pop, concave lid or intact seal does not prove adequate processing. No arbitrary recipe is made safe by substituting an invented pressure-canning time.

record.title: Jars, failed seals and pressure-canner operation
record.guidance: Use the selected tested process and equipment/lid directions. Where empty-jar presterilization is required, NCHFP specifies boiling water and elevation adjustment; 158 F is inadequate as the stated method. Pressure canners need ten minutes of free steam venting, correct altitude-adjusted operation, full processing time and natural cooling. If pressure drops, restart the full time. Seal failure requires prompt appropriate handling; eligible reprocessing uses a new lid and full correct process within 24 hours. This is not a rescue rule for initially unsafe food.

record.title: Drying is not a substitute for validated heating and endpoints
record.guidance: Use food-specific tested preparation, heating, drying and storage directions. Uncontrolled raw-meat sun drying and a 155 F air setting do not establish a safe internal heat treatment. Refrigerate jerky marination; do not infer a microbial kill from dryness, firmness or color. Outdoor sun drying is limited to suitable foods and favorable weather, rather than all meat and vegetables. Jerky shelf life cannot be inferred from the author’s months-long anecdote.

record.title: Salt-fish procedure has unresolved controls
record.guidance: The source omits a measured food-grade salt formulation, fish-specific handling, safe holding temperature, drying endpoint and validated keeping conditions. Rock or ice-cream-maker salt is not established as suitable for food by that description. The reviewer has not supplied a replacement salt-fish recipe; obtain a tested fish-specific method before use.

record.title: Reject oven dry canning
record.guidance: Do not use the book’s lidded-jar, twelve-hour oven process or reheat failed seals as a preservation method. NCHFP does not recommend oven or dry canning. Independently, the unit conversion is wrong: (200-32) times 5/9 is about 93.3 C, not 70 C. The author’s own lack-of-proof warning does not validate the procedure.

record.title: Pickles and ferments require food-specific controls
record.guidance: Retain tested food-to-liquid proportions and the recipe’s specified vinegar acidity, salt, temperature, fermentation completion, processing and storage requirements. Do not use tanginess or submersion alone as a safety test. The seven book ferments lack adequate process specifications; a small cabbage count is not a weight-based salt formulation. For comparison, F08 uses three tablespoons of salt per five pounds of shredded cabbage and describes about three to four weeks at 70-75 F, with its full handling and storage directions still required. This is a separate tested method, not a validated edit of the book recipe. The five quick-pickle recipes omit essential controls. Pickled eggs must be refrigerated; no recommended home-canning method makes these eggs pantry-stable.

record.title: Smoking and curing do not automatically make shelf-stable meat
record.guidance: Use a validated food-specific cure and process, the correct measured curing product and dose, refrigerated handling, an internal food thermometer and appropriate post-process storage. A premix is not self-dosing. Smoker-air temperature, dark color, a supposed impermeable pellicle or re-smoking a cut surface cannot demonstrate safety. USDA’s reviewed smoking-storage excerpt directs refrigeration within two hours, use within four days or freezing. No complete alternative shelf-stable curing recipe is supplied here.

record.title: Oxygen-reduced packaging is only for suitable dry foods
record.guidance: Do not equate absence of oxygen with absence of microbial hazards. USU warns about botulism with moist food in reduced-oxygen packages and describes about 10% or less moisture for this dry-storage context. That limit alone does not certify every product or a universal shelf life. Use known suitable food-contact containers, a food-appropriate packaging specification, clean equipment and manufacturer-sized absorbers. White color, a rat anecdote, a vacuum-cleaner hose or a nominal absorber size is not validation.

record.title: Measure cold storage and match the crop
record.guidance: A root cellar or evaporative cooler is not a refrigerator unless measured conditions support the food’s requirements. VCE calls for refrigerated food below 40 F; a 55 F claim is inadequate for general perishables. Match produce variety, humidity, temperature, curing and ventilation rather than treating the chart’s durations as guarantees. F15 describes very moist apple and pear storage rather than the book’s undefined medium humidity. UMN gives around 50-55 F for winter squash and pumpkins. The older WSU bulletin itself has different generalized and crop-specific squash ranges; these are not interchangeable universal prescriptions. Freezer burn concerns quality; it does not by itself make food unsafe.

record.title: Shelf life and date labels are conditional
record.guidance: Most commercial date labels concern quality, with infant formula an exception. Proper storage and the actual product matter. No seal or date establishes perpetual safety. For home-canned food, authoritative labeling, storage and best-quality guidance should be used instead of the book’s indefinite-life reassurance.

record.title: Avoid blanket anti-preservative and untested-GMO claims
record.guidance: FDA describes both antimicrobial and antioxidant preservative functions, rather than a merely cosmetic role. FDA, EPA and USDA have regulatory roles for genetically engineered foods, including FDA’s voluntary product-by-product consultation and submitted safety assessment data. These sources do not support the book’s blanket size-based harm argument or absence-of-assessment claim.

record.title: Underground storage sketches are not construction plans
record.guidance: Excavation, earth loads, drainage, access, structural support, materials and entrapment hazards remain unresolved. A block lining or buried refrigerator sketch is not evidence of a safe structure. Obtain a qualified site-specific design before construction; this examination does not determine permits or code compliance.

record.title: Home-rendered lard shelf stability is not established
record.guidance: The source supplies no validated moisture endpoint, process specification or storage study. Pale color does not resolve that gap. No universal room-temperature shelf life is assigned. Obtain a tested rendering and storage method, or qualified food-preservation advice; this examination does not assert that all properly rendered lard requires refrigeration.

record.title: Identification must establish the actual specimen
record.guidance: Common names, resemblance, an app, odor, a single feature, a photograph or confidence do not establish a safe meal. Learn complete local identification and toxic lookalikes with qualified help; reject uncertain specimens. Assess exact species, plant part, maturity and preparation. A small taste cannot clear unknown plants or demonstrate absence of allergy. None of this examination’s plant profiles is an approved field identification key.

record.title: No universal clean-site shortcut
record.guidance: Assess land use, treatment history, contamination and water/soil conditions. Uphill position, neglected growth, washing and a 100-foot road setback do not demonstrate toxin-free plants. EPA’s lead guidance concerns actual testing and exposure controls, not certification of every roadside or urban forage site.

record.title: Medicinal claims remain unvalidated
record.guidance: Food use, traditional use and laboratory activity are not proof of clinical efficacy or a safe medicinal dose. NCCIH finds no compelling dandelion efficacy evidence and inconsistent red-clover findings for several promoted uses. NCI does not support these foods/herbs as cancer treatment. Other specific herbal claims here were screened for gaps, not each exhaustively searched in clinical literature. Do not replace appropriate medical care with them; clinician review must address diagnosis, interactions, dose, age and pregnancy. No pediatric wine, wound poultice, botanical antibiotic or oral treatment has been approved by this examination.

record.title: Poisoning, bleeding and eye-treatment claims require proper care
record.guidance: Daylily juice is not an established arsenic antidote. In suspected poisoning, seek poison-control or emergency help without waiting for symptoms; do not use a homemade antidote. Internal bleeding, postpartum hemorrhage and serious cardiac symptoms need urgent clinical evaluation rather than herbal dosing. CDC identifies heavy postpartum bleeding and serious maternal heart symptoms as urgent warning signs. Homemade rose tea is not a sterile eye medicine; FDA requires ophthalmic medicines to be sterile. These constraints address particular claims; the reviewer does not claim to have validated every medical condition in this book.

record.title: Plantain does not replace snakebite care
record.guidance: Get medical help immediately for suspected venomous snakebite. CDC advises against folk therapies and attempts to remove venom. Reject plantain poultices and juice as an antidote; do not delay care to gather or prepare herbs.

record.title: Cyanogenic plants and unassessed plant parts
record.guidance: Chokecherry stems, leaves and seeds have cyanogenic hazards; the book’s bark remedies and incomplete human warning must remain held. The stated many-small-seeds description also needs botanical reconciliation rather than serving as a key. Bamboo needs species-appropriate preparation, including discarding cooking water under the cited FSANZ guidance. Its reassurance about commercial canned shoots does not endorse arbitrary home canning or raw shoot juice. Serviceberry seed tea and other nonfruit medicinal uses remain unassessed; no universal safe part or dose is inferred.

record.title: Mushroom shortcuts and cooking guarantees fail
record.guidance: Require expert identification of each mushroom; a hollow interior, white flesh, cap color, lack of gills or cooking alone cannot certify safety. FDA reports illness associated with true morels and says cooking cannot guarantee safety. False-morel toxins can persist after cooking. No mushroom entry in this book is promoted to a validated consumption protocol.

record.title: Correct scale, illustration and range errors
record.guidance: Plantain flowering stems are not seven to twenty feet tall; the consulted Extension description says under twelve inches.
